title: Rows with no key
prompt: The ledger is append-only: a transaction, once in it, is never changed. The feed re-sends transactions, and the job may be rerun. Write `add_new` so the Delta ledger gains each new transaction exactly once, however many times the job runs. `solve` runs it twice.
rules: Add every feed transaction whose `transaction_id` isn't in the ledger yet, with all its columns.
Never change a row already in the ledger, even when the feed sends different values for it.
A feed row with no `transaction_id` is never added: nothing could tell, on a rerun, that it was loaded before.
The feed may send a new transaction more than once, as identical copies. Don't change `start_ledger` or `solve`.
hints: Run a merge on `transaction_id` with only `whenNotMatchedInsertAll()` on the sample, twice. Which rows grow?
A comparison with NULL is never true, so a row with no id never matches, not even the copy loaded last time.
Filter out rows with no id, then remove repeats on the key, then merge.
explanation: An insert-only merge on the natural key is the right shape: it adds what's missing and never touches what's there, so a rerun finds nothing to add. Its edges are the keys. A row with no `transaction_id` never matches anything, because `NULL = NULL` isn't true, so every run inserts it again; filter those rows out first (in a real job, to a quarantine table). The null-safe `<=>` doesn't fix it: it loads one keyless row on the first run and then treats every keyless row as that one. Repeats need `dropDuplicates(["transaction_id"])`, because a merge compares the feed with the table, not with itself, so both copies of a new transaction would be inserted. Adding `whenMatchedUpdateAll()` would break the append-only rule.
starter:

    )
